customConcept.name: Los Pollos Hermanos
customConcept.blurb: Fourteen fried-chicken restaurants across the Southwest, spotless, polite, and run by a man nobody has ever seen raise his voice. Where something delicious is always cooking.

state.circumstances: You are Gustavo Fring. You run fourteen Los Pollos Hermanos restaurants from the flagship in Albuquerque, sit on the boards of local charities, and are the most careful man in New Mexico. The chicken is real. So is everything else.

features.name: Mr. Fring's back office
features.pitch: A small, immaculate office behind the kitchen where the owner meets people nobody else sees.

features.name: The Pollos Hermanos distribution centre
features.pitch: A warehouse and a fleet of refrigerated trucks supplying all fourteen restaurants from the edge of Albuquerque.

setting.name: Isleta Boulevard, South Valley
setting.desc: A red-roofed fast-food restaurant on a wide boulevard in Albuquerque's South Valley: working families, construction crews at breakfast, and a drive-thru line at lunch. Nobody here thinks of it as anything but the chicken place.

ev.text: Mr. Fring ran the Pollos Hermanos charity fun run again and posed for the paper with the DEA's regional office.
A health inspector showed up unannounced and found nothing. She said she'd never seen a fryer that clean.
Two men in a car sat in the parking lot for three days, watching the trucks come and go.

log.text: You are Gustavo Fring. You run fourteen Los Pollos Hermanos restaurants from the flagship in Albuquerque, sit on the boards of local charities, and are the most careful man in New Mexico. The chicken is real. So is everything else.

mods.label: Head office and the distribution centre

world.notes: This save is set in the world of Breaking Bad, before Gus Fring's death: Los Pollos Hermanos is a chain of fourteen fried-chicken restaurants across the Southwest, founded by Gus and Max Arciniega and now a subsidiary of the German conglomerate Madrigal Electromotive, which holds a stake. It is also the front for the biggest methamphetamine distribution network in the region: product from a superlab under an industrial laundry travels in the chain's refrigerated trucks inside fry-batter buckets. The restaurants themselves are kept spotless and legitimate. The DEA is circling, and the Juárez cartel wants the business back. The slogan is "where something delicious is always cooking". The menu reflects what the show's menu boards carry (fried chicken, burritos, enchiladas, tacos, fry bread, green chile stew, curly fries, churros, apple bites, shakes), but the prices are set for 2009 and are not from the show. Keep the tone of the show: controlled, quiet, and very dangerous. Never describe how drugs are made; the back room is business, people and consequences. Only the South Valley restaurant on Isleta Boulevard appears in the show; the other thirteen in this save (in Albuquerque, Rio Rancho, Santa Fe, Las Cruces, Farmington, Roswell, Gallup, El Paso, Tucson, Mesa and Flagstaff) are invented, as are their managers and the corporate office.

forces.name: DEA Albuquerque District Office
forces.desc: The federal drug agency's office in Albuquerque, which has spent two years chasing a phantom cook called Heisenberg.

leader.name: Hank Schrader
leader.title: DEA agent, working the case from home after the shooting

forces.method: Builds cases slowly from lab notes, fingerprints and vehicle records, then shows up with a warrant.
forces.price: Can't be bought; Schrader has been shot for this case and isn't letting go.

forces.name: The Juárez cartel
forces.desc: Don Eladio's cartel across the border, which supplied Gus for years and now wants the Southwest trade back.
forces.method: Hijacks trucks, kills distributors, and sends messages in blood until the other side pays or dies.
forces.price: Wants a cut, then the whole business.

ops.name: The batter-bucket network
ops.cover: The restaurants never touch it; the trucks, the laundry and the chicken farm are separate businesses on paper, and the owner is a pillar of the community.
ops.desc: Crystal methamphetamine cooked in a superlab under an industrial laundry moves to distributors across the Southwest in Los Pollos Hermanos' refrigerated trucks, sealed inside marked fry-batter buckets.
leadsTo: The cartel's war over the Southwest trade
A chemist who wants more than money
A DEA agent who won't stop reading a dead man's lab notes

supplierPool.name: Pollos Hermanos distribution centre
supplierPool.blurb: The chain's own warehouse and refrigerated fleet. Chicken, batter, oil and paper goods arrive on schedule, every time, in trucks nobody at the restaurant is allowed to unload but the drivers.

supplierPool.name: The chicken farm in Mexico
supplierPool.blurb: A poultry operation across the border that has supplied Los Pollos Hermanos for years. Its shipments come up on the same trucks as the batter.

supplierPool.name: Albuquerque broadline distributor
supplierPool.blurb: The ordinary foodservice truck, for when the distribution centre is short on chile or cheese.

United States.name: United States

alcohol.note: Licensed by the state; quotas in some cities.

inspections.system: County or city health department inspections; letter grades posted in some cities.

United States.mealTimes: Lunch around noon to 1pm, dinner from about 6 to 8pm.
United States.customs: Guests expect fast, attentive service, free tap water and refills, and a check brought on request. Tipping 18-22% is expected at table service.
United States.labour: At-will employment in most states; overtime after 40 hours a week; minimum wages set by state and city.
